title: ReSIDS event-stream scenario
description: Declarative description of a test scenario: which slice of the traffic stream to replay, the timing constants of the switching policy, and the scheduled membership changes. Replaces hard-coded schedules so a third party can reproduce an event stream from data + this file alone. The schedule is validated against the number of windows the selected stream actually has. Data and model bindings are pinned here too, so that data + this file + the emitted manifest reproduce a stream byte-for-byte.

name.description: Scenario id; names the output files.

stream.description: Which windows of the test stream to replay. 'benign_only' contains no attack sample, so every alarm in it is a false positive.

window_seconds.description: Round length; one round = one traffic window.

fusion_k.description: k in the k-of-n decision fusion.

detect_lag.description: Rounds from an inactivity event to the fail-fast FL->GL commanded by the NODE-LOCAL Disaster-FD monitor process, on local evidence only (no regional agreement), so it keeps fail-fast latency and partition tolerance.

dwell.description: Rounds of full membership required before the federated Disaster-FD considers the GL->FL return.

cmd_latency.description: Rounds the FEDERATED (regional) Disaster-FD takes to reach and issue a decision: GL->FL, isolation, losses while in GL. GL->FL has NO fallback: if the federation cannot decide, the system rests in GL.

watchdog.description: D: rounds the agent waits for its own node-local Disaster-FD monitor before falling back to FL->GL by itself. Used only when that local process is unavailable (local_fd_available: false). The fallback exists in the fail-safe direction only.

local_fd_available.description: Whether the node-local Disaster-FD monitor process is alive. true (normal): FL->GL is commanded by it (decided_by=monitor). false: models a crashed or hung local FD process, so the agent's watchdog fires after D rounds (decided_by=autonomous, reason=autonomous_fallback) -- the only case in which the agent acts on its own.

attribution.description: attack class -> emitter node. SYNTHETIC: source_node attribution does not exist in v2 (it is null); this is a v3 premise used to exercise the intrusion-driven driver.

escalate_flags.description: n_flags for an alarm to count as evidence against its source node.

isolate_after.description: Corroborated alarms attributed to one node before the MONITOR commands isolation.

command_switch_after.description: Isolations after which the monitor commands FL->GL. Intrusion never triggers the autonomous switch.

schedule.description: Membership changes, in rounds of this scenario's stream. Validated: every round must exist in the stream, and the up/down state machine must be consistent.

data.description: Input binding. Pinned here so the scenario, not the script, determines what is replayed.

benign_cap.description: subsample of the majority benign class (default 500000)

model.description: Everything that changes the trained specialists, hence the alarms. Pinned for reproducibility.

features_file.description: path to a features JSON carrying a 'features' list of 1-based F-numbers (e.g. features/all_in_one_ereno_train_combined.json)

sim_epoch.description: UTC anchor for the relative simulation time. SYNTHETIC: in deployment window_start/window_end come from the GOOSE/SV frame timestamps.
